# VERDICT: CONDITIONAL

Primary sources read: `human-review/dual-detector-paper/main.tex` (489 lines, full), `references.bib` (full), `main.pdf` (pages 1–2, 7–9, 11–13 rendered and compared line-by-line against the source).

---

## Findings

### 1. CRITICAL — A sentence in the Results is flatly false against the paper's own Table 2

**Location:** `main.tex:336`, §4.3, first sentence. Rendered PDF p. 8.

> "Across all three models, the dual detector outperforms either component alone."

Table 2 (`main.tex:281–284`, PDF p. 7) gives Llama-8B: **Geometry 0.912, Dual 0.880**. Dual loses on Llama by 0.032. The table itself **bolds 0.912** to mark geometry as the winner for that row, and the abstract independently says "Geometry alone reaches 0.912 on Llama-3.1-8B." The Results section contradicts a number bolded one page earlier.

The same overclaim recurs at `main.tex:418`, §5.2 opening: "The dual detector's superiority over either component reflects complementary information capture."

**Fix:** Replace with "On Mistral and Qwen the dual detector outperforms either component alone; on Llama, geometry alone is stronger (0.912 vs.\ 0.880 dual), which we do not interpret given overlapping CIs." Rewrite the §5.2 opener to not assert superiority as a premise — it is the thing being tested.

### 2. CRITICAL — §4.3's Δ values are silently taken from a different pipeline than the table they follow

**Location:** `main.tex:336`, §4.3.

> "On Mistral, the improvement is $\Delta = +0.078$ (geometry$\to$dual) and $\Delta = +0.061$ (entropy$\to$dual)."

These do not reconcile with Table 2, the table under discussion: 0.840 − 0.780 = **+0.060**, and 0.840 − 0.732 = **+0.108**. They reconcile exactly with **Table 3**, the uniform pipeline: 0.806 − 0.728 = +0.078, 0.806 − 0.745 = +0.061.

So the sentence names three models from Table 2, then reports deltas from Table 3, with no marker of the switch. A reader checking the arithmetic against Table 2 gets neither number.

**Fix:** State the source explicitly — "On the uniform pipeline (Table 3), the improvement is +0.078 / +0.061; on the kv\_verify pipeline (Table 2) it is +0.060 / +0.108." Do not report one without the other, since they disagree in ordering (entropy is the weaker channel in Table 2 and the stronger in Table 3).

### 3. CRITICAL — "All results survive [within-fold FWL / permutation tests]" is falsified by §4.6, inside the same Results section

**Location:** Abstract, `main.tex:68–72`; Conclusion, `main.tex:474`.

> "All results survive GroupKFold cross-validation by question domain, within-fold Frisch-Waugh-Lovell residualization of token count, and 1{,}000-iteration permutation tests"
> "…with all controls passing and all comparisons surviving Holm-Bonferroni correction."

§4.6 (`main.tex:383–392`, PDF p. 9) reports AUROC ≈0.69 and ≈0.33 obtained with **LOO and global FWL, explicitly pre-C2-fix**, with no permutation test and no CI — filed under the `\section{Results}` heading alongside the corrected numbers. This is the structural defect the brief names: a known-contaminated finding sitting under the same heading as the confirmed ones. It is *labeled* in prose (so not a silent correction), but position, not prose, is what a skimming reader reads.

Separately, "all controls passing" is false on Qwen (TC baseline 0.814, which the paper's own footnote calls "a substantial length confound") and questionable on Llama (Enc baseline 0.563 > TC baseline 0.504).

**Fix:** (a) Move §4.6 out of Results into an appendix or a subsection explicitly titled "Preliminary, superseded by C2 fix." (b) Abstract: "All *primary* results survive…". (c) Conclusion: scope "all controls passing" to Mistral-7B, or drop it — as written it reads globally and is false globally.

### 4. MAJOR — The Holm-Bonferroni family description is incompatible with Table 5

**Location:** `main.tex:254`, controls item 7.

> "The correction family includes all per-model AUROC tests (3 HEDGED-vs-CONFAB comparisons + 1 CORRECT-vs-CONFAB = 4 tests per model)… all observed raw $p$-values hit this floor, yielding identical adjusted $p = 0.004$"

The Holm arithmetic itself is correct (4 tied p-values at 1/1001 all adjust to 0.003996 ≈ 0.004). But the claim that *all four* tests per model hit the floor requires the CORRECT-vs-CONFAB test to be significant at p < 0.001 — while Table 5 reports Mistral entropy 0.756 with CI [0.356, 0.896] and **power 0.54**, and Llama with **power 0.05**. A permutation p at the floor and a BCa CI spanning chance for the same statistic at power 0.05 is not a reconcilable pair.

No p-value is reported anywhere in the paper. The claim is asserted, not shown.

**Fix:** Add a raw-p and adjusted-p column to Table 2 and Table 5. If the CORRECT-vs-CONFAB tests do not hit the floor, correct the sentence and recompute the adjusted values — with unequal p's Holm no longer yields identical 0.004 across the family, and the headline `p_adj = 0.004` in the abstract changes.

### 5. MAJOR — Zero data or code artifacts shipped; every number is unreproducible

`ls -laR human-review/dual-detector-paper/` returns exactly three files: `main.tex`, `main.pdf`, `references.bib`. No results JSON, no feature CSVs, no extraction or analysis code. There is no Data & Code Availability statement.

This is the defect already logged against `empathy-bus` in `ACTIVE_REVIEW.md` ("Zero shipped data artifacts"). The 5×6 cross-correlation matrix, the permutation-importance values, the power estimates, and every AUROC exist only as prose. I verified them for internal consistency only — I had nothing to verify them *against*.

**Fix:** Ship, at minimum: the per-trial feature table (200 rows × 11 features + label + domain + token count) per model, the behavioral-classifier script (both pre- and post-C1 versions, so the 76.7/79.2/60.0% audit is checkable), and the kv\_verify invocation. Add a Data & Code Availability section naming the paths. Also state the fixed random seed — §3.1 says "a fixed random seed" without giving it, so even the 200-question sample cannot be reconstructed.

### 6. MAJOR — Below-chance results are interpreted asymmetrically

**Location:** `main.tex:298` vs. `main.tex:374–381` / Table 5.

Mistral's encoding baseline of 0.373 — reported with **no CI** — gets a two-sentence mechanistic story ("encoding features weakly *anti-predict* generation-phase behavior… consistent with prior findings of encoding/generation sign reversal") and a self-citation.

Meanwhile Table 5's Llama entropy row is **0.240 with CI [0.043, 0.413]** — a confidence interval lying *entirely below chance*, the only interval in the paper that excludes 0.5 in that direction — and receives only the blanket caption "All comparisons are severely underpowered." Mistral's geometry value of 0.152 in the same table gets no CI and no comment at all.

A CI excluding chance is a finding. Giving a mechanism to the uncertainty-free 0.373 while filing the CI-excluding 0.240 under "underpowered" is reaching in one direction and shrugging in the other.

**Fix:** Either give CIs to the TC Base and Enc Base columns of Table 2 and interpret 0.373 only if its CI excludes 0.5, or delete the sign-reversal paragraph. And add one sentence to §4.5 addressing why entropy anti-predicts correctness on Llama with a CI excluding chance — "underpowered" does not cover it.

### 7. MAJOR — "differ slightly" understates a shift larger than the paper's headline effect

**Location:** Table 3 caption, `main.tex:311`.

> "Geometry/entropy/dual AUROCs differ slightly from \Cref{tab:main} because that table uses the full kv\_verify validation pipeline with different fold structure"

Actual shifts: geometry 0.780 → 0.728 (**0.052**), dual 0.840 → 0.806 (0.034), entropy 0.732 → 0.745 (0.013, opposite sign). The paper's central conclusion — text 0.820 "matches" dual 0.806 — rests on a **0.014** gap, four times smaller than the pipeline-to-pipeline movement in the same quantity. Table 3 carries no confidence intervals at all, so the reader has nothing to size that 0.014 against.

**Fix:** Drop "slightly." State the largest divergence numerically in the caption. Add BCa CIs to every row of Table 3 — without them "match" is an eyeball judgment on a difference smaller than the known instability.

### 8. MAJOR — Byline: AI authorship is undeclared and contribution roles are absent

**Location:** `main.tex:49–55`.

"Lyra" is first author with a `liberationlabs.tech` contact; the `\date` field carries "Analysis assisted by AI (Claude, Anthropic)." These two are in tension and the artifact does not resolve them: either Lyra *is* the Claude instance (making the assistance note redundant and the authorship undeclared), or Lyra is someone else. A venue reader cannot tell. Most target venues (ACL, NeurIPS, ICML) prohibit LLM authorship outright — this is a desk-reject trigger, not a style nit.

Additionally: no author-contributions statement. Wilkes's only stated contribution is "Statistical verification framework," which is the tool separately cited as `wilkes2026kv` — software authorship, not necessarily paper authorship. `ACTIVE_REVIEW.md` also lists Dwayne as a designated *reviewer* for this repo; being both byline author and named reviewer is a role conflict.

Burying the AI disclosure in the `\date` field is also the wrong location — it renders under the date line, above the abstract, formatted as an italic aside.

**Fix:** Add an explicit Author Contributions section using CRediT roles. State plainly which authors are AI systems. Move the AI-assistance disclosure out of `\date` into that section or a footnote on the title. Obtain and record written sign-off from Edrington and Wilkes before this ships.

### 9. MINOR — §4.1 Qwen power range excludes its own worst row

**Location:** `main.tex:302`. "Qwen is severely underpowered (power~0.40--0.71)."

Table 2 gives Qwen powers of 0.40, **0.17**, and 0.71. The stated range omits the entropy row and understates how underpowered Qwen is. **Fix:** "power 0.17–0.71."

### 10. MINOR — §4.1 "CI lower bounds touch chance" is wrong for two of three rows

**Location:** `main.tex:302`. Qwen CIs are Geometry [0.437, …], Entropy [0.390, …], Dual [0.500, …]. Only Dual *touches* 0.5; the other two are below it. The table footnote gets this right ("CIs span chance"); the prose is weaker than the footnote. **Fix:** "The CI lower bounds fall at or below chance for all comparisons."

### 11. MINOR — Table 5 column ownership is recoverable only from prose, and row order breaks with Table 2

**Location:** `main.tex:370–378`.

Header is `Model | N (C/F) | Entropy | CI | Geometry | Power`. The CI column sits between two AUROC columns; nothing in the header or caption says which it belongs to — only §4.5's prose ("the Mistral entropy result… the CI spans chance") resolves it. Geometry has no CI; "Power" is unattributed to either channel. Row order is Mistral/Qwen/Llama, whereas Table 2 is Mistral/Llama/Qwen.

**Fix:** Rename to "Entropy AUROC" / "Entropy CI" / "Geometry AUROC" / "Geometry CI" / "Power (entropy)". Reorder rows to match Table 2.

### 12. MINOR — The AMBIGUOUS class is defined but never counted, and class counts do not sum to 200

§3.2 defines four categories. AMBIGUOUS appears exactly once in the paper and is never given an N. Reconstructing: Mistral 32+149+10 = 191 (9 unaccounted), Llama 157+34+6 = 197 (3), Qwen 7+174+10 = 191 (9). A reader cannot check that the classes partition the sample.

Related: the precedence rule is unstated. HEDGED is defined by markers, CORRECT by string match — a hedged response containing the correct answer satisfies both, and which label wins determines the composition of the HEDGED class, which is the numerator of the headline comparison. For a paper whose thesis is "audit your classifier," this omission is pointed.

**Fix:** Add a class-count table (all four categories × three models, summing to 200) and state the label precedence order explicitly.

### 13. MINOR — Permutation-importance sign convention reads backwards

**Location:** `main.tex:429`. "$\Delta$AUROC $= +0.083$ when shuffled." Permutation importance is the *drop* when a feature is shuffled; a positive Δ reads as an increase. **Fix:** "AUROC drops by 0.083 when shuffled" or use negative signs consistently.

### 14. MINOR — "mean 0.089" is undefined as signed or absolute

Abstract and §5.2 report "max $|r| = 0.206$, mean 0.089." A signed mean near zero and a mean of absolute values carry opposite implications for complementarity. **Fix:** "mean $|r| = 0.089$." Also expand "TC Base" / "Enc Base" in the Table 2 caption — neither abbreviation is defined anywhere.

---

## Known kills — checked and clear

- **STALE_PDF: clear.** `main.tex` mtime Apr 20 16:43, `main.pdf` 16:44. I compared rendered pages 1–2, 7–9, and 11–13 against source: title block, abstract, contributions, Tables 2/3/4/5 (every cell), §4.1–4.6, §5.2–5.5, Conclusion, both first-person boxes, and the bibliography all match the `.tex` exactly. Cross-references resolve (Contribution 3 → "Section 5.2", `tab:main` → "Table 2").
- **Orphaned / dangling bib entries: clear.** 13 keys cited, 13 entries present, one-to-one. No orphans, no dangling keys.
- **Fabricated author names: no evidence of fabrication.** All eleven external entries match publications I can identify (Ji et al. ACM CSUR 55(12); Kadavath arXiv 2207.05221; Manakul arXiv 2303.08896; Wei et al. arXiv 2411.04368; Marks & Tegmark CoLM 2024; Marchenko & Pastur Mat. Sb. 1967). Note `wei2024simpleqa` renders "Nguyen Karina" — that is correct, not a swapped name.
- **Positional footnote/cross-reference rot: clear.** Table 2's `†` anchors to the row label "Qwen-7B" and its `*` to the value "0.814"; Table 3's `†` anchors to "Hedge count only." All name the row or the value, none say "line 4." No positional references anywhere in the source.
- **Silent correction: clear.** C1 and C2 are both given their own labeled subsections stating what was wrong, the magnitude (Table 1: 76.7/79.2/60.0%, arithmetic verified correct against the raw counts), and what changed. §5.4.1 even states the number the bug would have produced (0.601). This is the paper's strongest feature.

---

## What I could NOT check

1. **Twin edition — no twin exists in reach, and I could not confirm one doesn't exist elsewhere.** `human-review/dual-detector-paper/` contains exactly three files; there is no `academic/` subdirectory. **I could not read `C:\Users\Thomas\Desktop\LiberationLabs\Research\published-research\`** — Grep, Glob, and Read were all denied on that tree (session is scoped to `tools/agni` and `human-review`). `ACTIVE_REVIEW.md` states this paper was among ten that "existed only" in `lyra-s-research-`, which argues against a downstream twin, but **that is a secondary description and I am not treating it as verification.** TWIN_DESYNC is **UNVERIFIED**. To check: read access to `published-research/` and to the `lyra-s-research-` repo.

2. **Downstream citation integrity — UNVERIFIED.** `ACTIVE_REVIEW.md` records that this paper is already **cited** as "source of the gated SimpleQA 0.840 figure and a body-count row in meta-pattern," while its own status line reads *unreviewed* — never through an Agni gate or human pass. I could not read `published-research\meta-pattern\main.tex` or its `references.bib` to check whether meta-pattern cites the post-C1 0.840 or a pre-fix number, or whether the "body-count row" reflects the corrected 10/149 counts. **Recommend holding the meta-pattern citation until this is checked.** To check: read access to `published-research/meta-pattern/`.

3. **Dead URLs — UNVERIFIED.** WebFetch was denied. The two URLs in the reference list are unchecked: `https://zenodo.org/records/19479624` (`edrington2026detecting`) and `https://github.com/DwayneWilkes/KV-Experiments` (`wilkes2026kv`). The second matters more than usual — it is the sole citation for the statistical framework producing every number in the paper, and no local copy of kv\_verify is shipped. To check: network access, or a local vendored copy of kv\_verify.

4. **Every empirical number — UNVERIFIED against source.** With no data or code in the directory (Finding 5), I checked all values for *internal* consistency only: cross-table agreement, arithmetic (C1 contamination percentages, Holm adjustment, hedge rates, Δ derivations, feature counts). I verified nothing against a primary data artifact. The AUROCs, CIs, power estimates, R²/ρ values, the 5×6 cross-correlation matrix, and the permutation-importance figures are all unaudited. To check: the per-trial feature tables and the analysis scripts.

5. **Author sign-off — UNVERIFIED.** I have no record that Thomas Edrington or Dwayne Wilkes has approved this byline or this draft. To check: written confirmation from each.

6. **Git history — not available.** `git -C human-review log -- dual-detector-paper` required approval and was denied, so I could not check whether an earlier edition, a retracted claim, or a second PDF exists in history.

---

**Conditions to clear before ship:** Findings 1, 2, and 3 are false statements in the artifact and are blocking. Finding 4 requires either reported p-values or a corrected family description — the abstract's `p_adj = 0.004` depends on it. Finding 5 (ship the data) and Finding 8 (declare AI authorship, add contributions, obtain sign-off) are blocking for any external venue. Findings 6 and 7 are blocking for a methods-focused venue. The rest are editorial.
